## Spec conformance

SPEC §3 T14: *"`texture_worker.js` (transcode + terrain assembly + NRA derive), results-enqueue-only integration, FIFO fallback arm retained verbatim. Acceptance: GATE-TEXWORKER — TAIL-ULTRA worker-vs-FIFO arms (transcode bucket), BOOT-WARM queue depth; no eye item (same transcoder, same output). Kill: worker-arm tail worse than FIFO arm, or fallback failing to engage silently+counted."*

- **`texture_worker.js` — transcode + terrain assembly + NRA derive** — **MET.** All three job kinds implemented per the pass-05 S3 contract (one transferable in / one out, `parseHbc7`-shaped reconstruction main-side, FIFO one-at-a-time, cancel by seq, ready never waits on the lazy transcoder). NRA finding per the task brief: the runtime today derives normal/height (and roughness/AO for texchan-class use) **wasm-side** in `crates/holtburger-dat/src/normal_gen.rs` from decoded RGBA8 (`SurfacePixels.normalPixels`, adapter.js:1162–1200 wraps it; both call sites strength 1.0), while terrain nra is baked offline — so the port target was normal_gen.rs, ported strict-f32 and proven byte-identical against goldens generated by the Rust source itself (41/41).
- **Results-enqueue-only integration** — **MET.** The worker fetches nothing (bytes handed in by the main thread) and creates no GPU objects; arrival callbacks only settle promises (the same microtask shape as the FIFO's `job.resolve`); uploads keep today's schedule (terrain array still `needsUpdate=true` → driver pays at next bind; singleton path unchanged). Full pass-08 P4/W2 staging via `initTexture` is ST8/ST9 scope, not T14's.
- **FIFO fallback arm retained verbatim** — **MET.** `?xu7Budget` machinery untouched (`_drain`/`_scheduleDrain`/stats byte-identical; `transcodeXu7` gained only the flag-gated worker-first branch). `test_xu7_budget.mjs` 49/49 green unmodified.
- **Fallback engages automatically, counted, never silent (kill criterion)** — **MET.** Construction failure, crash mid-job, not-ready, over-cap, dead-worker terrain, and per-record job errors each resolve the caller (FIFO or hbc7-route/re-fetch contracts) AND increment a dedicated `__texWorkerStats` counter with a one-shot console.warn — the full matrix is pinned by test (PART 6, 15 checks).
- **No eye item (same transcoder, same output)** — **MET, in node (no chromium needed).** The task allowed a browser smoke if basisu couldn't run in node; it can (`createRequire` UMD branch, test_xu7_transcode precedent), so byte-identity is asserted twice: mock-transcoder end-to-end through the real client+handler, and REAL transcoder × real 2048² corpus payload × two independent instances — byte-identical BC7 both times. Terrain: worker-assembled arrays byte-identical to `buildTerrainBc7Array`'s mipmaps with identical texture flags.
- **GATE-TEXWORKER (TAIL-ULTRA worker-vs-FIFO transcode bucket; BOOT-WARM queue depth)** — **DEFERRED-TO-BATCH** (per the task brief: 1070 arms are owner-batch items). Bench-ready wiring landed: `?texWorkers=on|0|N` explicit arms, `__texWorkerStats` queue-depth/in-flight/msTranscode/fallback counters (the pass-05 Q4 one-worker-sufficiency reading is `maxQueueDepth` on a warm boot), and the §0 url-flags row records the flip criteria. No 1070 numbers are claimed; the one timing pair printed by the real-transcoder suite is labeled informational (same box, second-instance warm-up — not an arm comparison).
- **Flag lifecycle (I7)** — **MET.** DEFAULT-OFF DEV opt-in; OFF arm verified byte-identical legacy behavior (all four pre-existing texture-family suites green; flag-off never constructs the worker or reads `import.meta`-URL beyond module load).

## Deviations

None against SPEC.md. Three sub-spec notes (refinements within the contract, recorded per I3's spirit):

1. **Pass-05 S3's flag sentence says "`?texWorkers=0|1|N` (default 1)"** while SPEC §3 T14 + the protocol header I7 say the flag lands DEFAULT-OFF. SPEC wins (§0.1: pass files are rationale): shipped as DEFAULT-OFF exact-match opt-in; `N>1` reads ON, is recorded in diag (`requested`), and still constructs ONE worker (S3 marks N>1 measurement-only; a second worker is explicitly gated on the pass-05 Q4 warm-boot queue-depth measurement).
2. **`ready` handshake message** — pass-05 S3 lists no ready ack for the texture worker; pass-08's bake-worker vocabulary has one and the client needs a construction-success signal for the counted-fallback contract. Added `{type:"ready"}` (answering `init`), which never waits on the transcoder.
3. **Crash mid-job loses the transferred payload bytes** — pending jobs resolve null (xu7 ⇒ the existing hbc7-route fallback = correct pixels at extra wire cost; terrain ⇒ re-fetch from the immutable HTTP cache). Counted (`pendingNulled`) and warned. The alternative (retaining a copy of every in-flight payload) buys retry-without-refetch at a transient double-buffer cost; not taken for a crash-only path.

## Handoffs & risks

- **ST5 (T15) consumes:** `want.nra` on xu7 jobs + `workerDeriveNra()` (both landed, tested, zero production callers at ST4 — `transcodeXu7` sends `want:{nra:null}`); `cancelTextureWorkerJob(seq)` is the eviction seam; `__texWorkerStats` folds into `__texStats().worker` at ST5 (registry successor edge already encoded — land the full `__texStats` schema there, don't extend this surface).
- **ST-SHELL (T11):** the worker is a 5th esbuild entry (`texture_worker` is already named in SPEC §1.1's entry list); the worker fetches `scene3d/transcoder/basis_transcoder.{js,wasm}` by stable name relative to `import.meta.url` — T02's F-15 hash-vs-stable naming decision applies to the WORKER's copy too.
- **1070 batch (T30-class):** GATE-TEXWORKER arms are prepared (`?texWorkers=on` vs `=0`, TAIL-ULTRA transcode bucket via the stall probe + `__texWorkerStats`; BOOT-WARM `maxQueueDepth` answers pass-05 Q4 before anyone builds `?texWorkers=2`).
- **Risk — terrain ready-wait:** the 10 s bound [A] on the one-shot terrain assembly is untuned; on a pathological line the worker-script fetch could exceed it ⇒ counted `terrainFallbacks` + today's synchronous build (i.e., today's behavior). Bench data can shrink it.
- **Risk — helper duplication:** `texture_worker.js` duplicates `parseHbc7`/`bc7LevelBytes` (import-map constraint). Drift is pinned by test PART 2, but a future HBC7 v3 change must touch both files — the worker's header says so.
- **Unrelated dirty files:** T10's WIP (`apps/holtburger-tools/**`, `crates/holtburger-manifest/**`, `crates/holtburger-dat/src/walk.rs`, `scripts/serve.py`, `Cargo.lock`) left staged-out per I6; `impl/task-T10-report.md` appeared untracked during this task (T10's, untouched).
